paragraphs: I'm applying for the Strategic Finance Manager role at Jerry. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters before that. What caught my attention is how you framed the hire: each dollar committed to a product line, a marketing channel or a headcount is a dollar not available elsewhere. That question is what most of my work has been about.

At JPMorgan Asset Management I worked on budget allocation across marketing channels. I built models to evaluate how to deploy $10M, benchmarked past allocations to find 30% in efficiency gains, and moved funding away from underperforming channels, which drove a 1.5x increase in performance metrics. At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%, and I ran variance and sensitivity analyses on budget changes. Before that, at Thomson Reuters, I supported monthly P&L forecasting, variance analysis and close for the ANZ region.

That lines up with the operating model, forecast cycle and channel economics you want this person to own. I should be upfront that I come to this from corporate finance and analytics, not from a bank or a PE firm, and my valuation work (DCF, comps and an LBO on J.M. Smucker) is MBA coursework. I check my own numbers and I write plainly for senior leaders. I'd welcome the chance to talk about the role.
